_doc: Marker vocabulary for the trader-facing claim provenance guard.
ONE file, TWO readers: src/test/claimProvenance.test.ts and
backend/tests/test_claim_provenance.py. It is not duplicated per lane on
purpose - a vocabulary copied into two places is the exact failure this
repo has already paid for once (pattern names drifting across four copies).
WHAT THIS GUARDS. A trader-facing assertion about the world that cannot be
derived from that trader's own trades and carries no citable source. It is
NOT a ban on numbers: %, rupees, multipliers and trader-specific metrics are
the product's whole job. Every pattern below is a CLAIM SHAPE, and not one
of them matches a bare numeral. The claim that started this guard -
'Proven pattern disruption to stop cascade losses' - contains no digit at
all, and two manual audits searching for numbers walked straight past it.
Patterns must parse in BOTH JavaScript RegExp and Python re: no lookbehind,
no named groups, no possessives. Matching is case-insensitive, LINE BY LINE
over the file with comments stripped first (quoting a removed claim in a
comment is a repo idiom and must not fail the build). It matched string
literals only until 2026-09-03, when that extractor was found to go blind
after an apostrophe in JSX prose - see the test docstring.

population.why: A claim about traders in general. The product observes ONE trader and has no population to speak for. Note `them` was removed from the alternation on 2026-09-03: "you won 62% of them" is the trader's OWN record and is exactly the kind of derived figure this product exists to show.

authority.why: Borrowed credibility. Every such claim audited on 2026-09-03 (26 of them) resolved to no source; the SEBI attributions were measurably wrong about what SEBI publishes. Note the SEBI patterns require an ATTRIBUTION verb or a data noun - naming the regulator is legitimate and constant in this product ('Not SEBI registered', 'SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013'). A bare \bSEBI\b marker returned eight legal-disclaimer hits and would have forced them into the allowlist, which is how a guard like this rots.

counterfactual_money.why: Already banned by the product's own rule: behaviour-to-money is the REALISED P&L of flagged trades, never a saving that cannot be observed. This makes the rule executable.

multiplier_or_correlation.why: A ratio or association asserted as established fact. The '2.7x faster' on the Dashboard was attributed to SEBI, is actually Odean 1998 at ~1.5x, and pointed the OPPOSITE way to this book's own measurement.

prediction.why: The charter is explicit: an alert converts an automatic action into a deliberate one, it does NOT predict. Note there is deliberately no /predict/ pattern - honest copy says 'TradeMentor does not predict your next trade'.

_why: A DIFFERENT CLASS from marker_groups above. Those match claims about the
WORLD - statistics, borrowed authority, forecasts. These match claims
about the PRODUCT: that it blocks, enforces, guarantees, or acts on the
trader's behalf.
Added 2026-09-03 after the guard missed one. 'Circuit breaker prompts
suggesting a cooldown period' sat live on the landing page: no digit, no
statistic, no authority - and flatly false, because nothing in this
product blocks a trade and the philosophy is mirror-not-blocker. It was
found by hand from an old backlog, not by this file.
Checked ONLY on scope.frontend.marketing_surfaces, and that is a
measured decision rather than caution. Run repo-wide these markers
returned 6 hits and ALL SIX were legitimate: a real Kite API circuit
breaker and its log lines, a 'non-blocking' refresh message, accurate
opt-in rule copy in the onboarding wizard, and two internal comments. On
the marketing surfaces they return zero. A guard that is 100% noise
where it is broad and silent where it is narrow belongs in the narrow
place.
Marketing surfaces must not sell a detector that no longer exists. The
landing page was demonstrating `Early Exit` and `Meltdown Cascade` a day
after both were retired. Checked ONLY on the surfaces listed under
scope.frontend.marketing_surfaces - several of these labels are ordinary
English ('Holding a loser') and are legitimate anywhere a stored alert
row is rendered.

frontend._exclude_why: _archive is already outside typecheck and eslint. components/ui is vendored shadcn. /test/ is this guard and its neighbours, which quote claims in order to assert on them.

backend._why: Not all of backend/app. A broad scan returned 31 hits of which 28 were docstrings, log lines and 'saved to history' - a guard at 10% precision gets muted. These are the modules that emit text a trader can actually read.
